definition: Continuing to train a pre-trained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset so it adapts to a target domain.
details: Fine-tuning exploits features learned during pre-training and adapts them to a new task with far less data than training from scratch. The ULMFiT recipe showed that a language-model “head” trained on a corpus could be fine-tuned layer by layer for text classification, and this pattern — pre-train broadly, fine-tune narrowly — underlies most applied NLP.

explainer.lead: Fine-tuning gives an already-trained model a focused education for a particular job. By building on what it learned during pre-training, it can adapt to a new task with much less data than training from the beginning.

tiers.eli5: Imagine someone who has read lots of books and then practises one specific kind of puzzle. They do not have to learn reading all over again; they use what they already know to get better at the puzzle. Fine-tuning does something similar by giving a broadly trained model extra practice on examples for one task.
tiers.practitioner: Start with a pre-trained model and continue training it on a smaller dataset for the target task, rather than initialising a new model from scratch. For language-model classifiers, the ULMFiT recipe fine-tunes the pre-trained language-model head layer by layer. Task-specific training data is still required.
tiers.paperLevel: Given pre-trained parameters θ0 and a task-specific dataset D_task, fine-tuning continues optimisation from θ0 on D_task to adapt the model to the target domain. ULMFiT instantiated this approach by fine-tuning a corpus-trained language-model head layer by layer for text classification. Its advantage over training from scratch is reuse of pre-trained features with substantially less task data.

explainer.example: A language-model head is first trained on a broad corpus. It is then fine-tuned layer by layer on a smaller set of reviews labelled as positive or negative, following the ULMFiT pattern, to produce a text classifier without training a language model from scratch.

usedIn.name: Applied natural language processing
usedIn.detail: The pattern of broad pre-training followed by narrow fine-tuning underlies most applied NLP.

explainer.intuition: Pre-training supplies broadly useful features, and fine-tuning adjusts them for a narrower purpose. This reuses earlier learning instead of making the target task teach the model everything from zero.
howItWorks: Pre-train a model on a broad corpus or dataset.
Choose a smaller dataset for the target task or domain.
Initialise training with the pre-trained model rather than random parameters.
Continue training on the task data, adapting the learned features.
Use the resulting model for the target task.
explainer.whyItMatters: Fine-tuning makes pre-trained features useful for new tasks while requiring far less task data than training from scratch. Pre-train broadly and fine-tune narrowly has become a foundational pattern in applied NLP.
misconceptions: Fine-tuning is not training from scratch: it begins with a pre-trained model.
It is not the same as broad pre-training: its dataset is smaller and task-specific.
It does not eliminate the need for data: examples for the target task are still used.
